thesis: Method: across all 14 catalog managers' filings public by 2026-02-13 (as_of filters on filing date, never period), I counted how many independently hold each of the 43 tradeable roster tickers, mapping CUSIP to ticker via the repo's own ledger bridge. Two managers were excluded from that count before anything else: RENTECH (3,185 total positions) and BRIDGEWATER (1,040) individually cover 51% and 63% of the entire 43-name roster -- a name appearing in either book is barely more informative than a coin flip, because these two own almost everything liquid. The remaining 12 'selective' managers cover a mean of 15.3% of the roster each (range 0%-33%, BRK/PERSHING/SCION/ELLIOTT near zero, ARKINVEST/COATUE near a third), which is a plausible base rate for actual selection rather than near-universal coverage, so I built the crowding score from those 12 only. Mapping loss, reported as instructed: 5,071 raw holdings across all 14 managers, 220 (4.3%) resolved to any ticker via CUSIP, and 4,851 (95.7%) did not -- expected, per the addendum, because the bridge only knows CUSIPs the user has personally traded, not a general CUSIP directory. Of the 220 mapped rows, 128 fall on the 43-symbol roster. That means this whole exercise runs on a narrow, ledger-biased slice: 'crowded' here means 'held by several selective managers AND already something the user has owned or watched,' not 'crowded across the market.' Staleness, exactly as the addendum's table states: 10 of the 12 selective managers (BRK, PERSHING, SCION, APPALOOSA, DUQUESNE, THIRDPOINT, ELLIOTT, TIGERGLOBAL, COATUE, LONEPINE) show Q3-2025 positions, 140 days stale at trade start (2026-02-17); ARKINVEST and SOROS show Q4-2025, 48 days stale. Sign test, as instructed: I computed trailing 3-month, 6-month and 1-year returns through the design cutoff for the 24 roster tickers that any selective manager held (crowding score 1-10), and correlated (Spearman, rank-based, robust to the one extreme outlier SNDK, a +1,242% 6-month move) against the crowding score. Results: 3m rho=+0.24 (all 24) / +0.36 (excl. SNDK); 6m rho=+0.17 / +0.27; 1y rho=+0.25 (n=23). All positive, none large, and the critical value for significance at n~23 (two-sided, alpha=0.05) is about 0.41 -- not one of these clears it, with or without the outlier. A high-crowd (score>=5, n=6: AMZN TSM META MSFT GOOGL NVDA) vs low-crowd (score<=2, n=12-13) bucket split tells an inconsistent story across windows: high beat low on 3m (-1.2% vs -8.2% all-24, -1.2% vs -19.0% ex-SNDK) but roughly matched or lagged on 6m and 1y once the SNDK outlier moves out of the low bucket. That is 'neither, convincingly' -- 14 managers filtered down to 11-24 overlapping names is nowhere near enough independent information to separate 'many good investors converged for a reason' from 'a crowded trade has no marginal buyer left,' and I am not going to assert a direction the data does not support. What I did about it: I do not use crowding to rank, size, or time entries -- I use it only as the addendum requires, as a universe filter, and treat the sign question as unresolved rather than pick one to sound decisive. The investable universe is every ticker with a crowding score >=3 (at least 3 of the 12 selective, independent processes hold it): AMD AMZN AVGO GOOGL META MSFT NFLX NVDA TSLA TSM UNH -- 11 names, dropping the crowd-1/2 tickers (idiosyncratic single- or double-manager bets, no more informative than an arbitrary stock pick) and the giants' contribution. Timing is carried entirely by price, per the addendum's own constraint that the DSL has no 13F terms: enter on a confirmed uptrend that is not already extended (close above both its 50- and 150-day averages, RSI(14) under 70, so the entry lags a fresh breakout rather than chasing one), exit on trend break or momentum fade (close below its 50-day average, or RSI(14) under 40). Mechanism, for whichever story turns out true: if this is validation, buying only names multiple independent, well-resourced processes already own, and only once price itself confirms the trend, should see fewer false starts than an unfiltered momentum screen; if it is fragility, the same filter is buying into names with the least room for a new buyer, and the trend-break exit is the only defence available, on the same delayed, close-based trigger every card in this tournament has to accept. On the other side of every entry: momentum traders already positioned before the RSI/sma filter confirms, and anyone who sold into a crowded name expecting exactly the fragility story to play out. Two engine limits I am not working around: this is a single frozen snapshot for the whole six-month window -- a real 13F strategy would refresh at the Q4-2025 stragglers (~2026-02-17) and Q1-2026 filings (~2026-05-15), both inside the trading window, and this engine cannot rotate a universe mid-run, so treat this as one stale six-month bet, not a live 13F strategy. And stop_loss_pct/position_pct are single fixed numbers: ATR(14)/close across these 11 names at 2026-02-13 ranges from 3.3% (NFLX) to 7.1% (AMD), mean 4.4%, so the 10% stop below is roughly 2.3x the average name's daily range but only ~1.4x AMD's -- AMD and TSLA (ann. vol 62-64%) are the volatility-mismatched names in an otherwise 26-51% ann.-vol universe, and I am keeping them in rather than quietly dropping the two names crowding independently flagged.
entry: close > sma(50) and close > sma(150) and rsi(14) < 70
